lines: In Australia, scientists studied a small animal called the quoll.
They discovered how quolls learn from each other.
This animal was in danger because of the cane toad, a species that was introduced to Australia in the 1930s.
To the quolls, it looked like tasty food, but it was very poisonous.
Many quolls that ate cane toads died quickly.
To solve this problem, scientists used the quolls’ natural behavior of copying others.
Scientists gave the quolls special sausages made from cane toads.
These sausages were harmless and safe, but a chemical in them did make the quolls feel sick after eating them.
So the quolls learned to stay away from cane toads.
Then the scientists let the trained quolls return to the wild.
These smart quolls showed their babies what they learned.
Other wild quolls copied this safe behavior, too.
This kind of behavior is called social learning.
As more baby quolls learned not to eat the dangerous toads, more quolls survived.
The number of dead quolls went down.
As a result, the quolls were able to survive without much help from humans.
Their natural copying behavior saved them.
